class.name: PhysXTank3D
class.brief_description: A PhysX-specific tracked (tank-style) vehicle, powered by PxVehicle2 -- the same real per-wheel suspension/tire/drivetrain composition [PhysXVehicle3D] and [PhysXMotorcycle3D] offer, driven entirely by skid-steer instead of a throttle+steer pair.
class.description: PxVehicle2 has no track/tank primitive of its own. Every wheel is driven and none steer; instead, each wheel's own throttle response is set independently every tick from [member left_ratio]/[member right_ratio], so the two sides of the vehicle can spin in genuinely opposite directions at once for a real pivot turn. Node structure mirrors [PhysXVehicle3D]/[PhysXMotorcycle3D]: add a [CollisionShape3D] child with a [BoxShape3D] for the hull, and 2 to 16 [PhysXVehicleWheel3D] children. Which track a wheel belongs to is inferred automatically from its own local X position sign (negative = left, positive = right) -- there is no explicit per-wheel track-side property, and [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.use_as_steering]/[member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.use_as_traction] are unused on a tank's wheels. Each wheel's own [member Node3D.position] is where it rests under static load, same convention [PhysXVehicle3D]'s wheels use. Drive it every physics tick by setting [member left_ratio], [member right_ratio], and [member brake]. Unlike [member PhysXVehicle3D.throttle]/[member PhysXMotorcycle3D.throttle] ([code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code], direction chosen by a separate reverse gear), [member left_ratio]/[member right_ratio] are signed ([code]-1[/code] to [code]1[/code]): the sign is the direction, so a track can drive forward, reverse, or (with the two tracks at opposite signs) pivot in place, all without a gear change. Only runs in an actual running game, never in the editor -- placing or moving the node in the Inspector does not simulate or fall under gravity.

method.name: get_actor_position
method.description: The real PhysX actor's own world-space origin -- for comparing against this node's own [member Node3D.global_position] (which tracks the same point) when diagnosing a suspension/placement issue.

method.name: get_angular_velocity
method.description: Current world-space angular velocity of the hull.

method.name: get_forward
method.description: Current world-space forward direction of the hull.

method.name: get_forward_speed
method.description: Current speed along the hull's own forward axis, in m/s. Positive while driving forward, negative while driving backward.

method.name: get_linear_velocity
method.description: Current world-space linear velocity of the hull.

method.name: get_up
method.description: Current world-space up direction of the hull.

method.name: get_wheel_jounce
method.description: How compressed wheel [param wheel]'s suspension is right now, from [code]0[/code] (fully extended / max droop) to that wheel's own [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel] (fully compressed / bottomed out). [param wheel] is the child index among this node's [PhysXVehicleWheel3D] children, in the order they were added.

method.name: get_wheel_separation
method.description: [code]0[/code] when wheel [param wheel] can reach the ground within its suspension travel. A negative value means the wheel is penetrating the ground even at full compression -- [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel] is too short for the current ride height. [param wheel] uses the same child-index convention as [method get_wheel_jounce].

method.name: is_sleeping
method.description: Returns whether the underlying PhysX vehicle actor is currently sleeping.

members.member: Brake pedal input, [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Scales up to [member max_brake_torque] of braking torque at each wheel, on both tracks at once. Set every physics tick from script; does not persist on its own the way a real pedal would.

Whether the vehicle is allowed to sleep after remaining below the PhysX space's configured sleep thresholds. The global [code]physics/physx_3d/simulation/allow_sleep[/code] project setting can disable sleeping for all PhysX bodies.

The vehicle center of mass in the vehicle's local coordinates when [member center_of_mass_mode] is [code]Custom[/code]. In [code]Auto[/code] mode, the center of mass follows the hull [CollisionShape3D] child position.
Whether to derive the center of mass from the hull [CollisionShape3D] position ([code]Auto[/code]) or use [member center_of_mass] directly ([code]Custom[/code]).

Same meaning as [member CollisionObject3D.collision_layer]. Applies to the hull only -- the wheels do not have their own collision shapes (their ground contact is handled entirely by the suspension, not by a physical wheel shape touching the road).

Same meaning as [member CollisionObject3D.collision_mask]. Applies to the hull box and to what the wheels' own ground raycasts can rest on: a wheel only hits non-area shapes on a layer in this mask (like a [RayCast3D]), so it never rests on an [Area3D]. See [member collision_layer].

Drive input for the left track, [code]-1[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Scales up to [member max_engine_torque] of drive torque, split evenly across the left track's own wheels; sign is direction, not a separate reverse gear. Set every physics tick from script.
Total mass of the tank, in kg.

The braking torque applied to each wheel when [member brake] is [code]1[/code]. Higher values stop the wheel's own rotation faster, but do not by themselves determine whether the tire skids once locked -- see [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.tire_friction] for that.
The total drive torque a fully-throttled track produces, split evenly across that track's own wheels -- see [member left_ratio]/[member right_ratio].
The vehicle's own rotational inertia around its X/Y/Z axes. Higher values resist rotation (pitch/yaw/roll) more.

Contact material of the hull box (the property [RigidBody3D] and [VehicleBody3D] use): its friction, [i]rough[/i], bounce and [i]absorbent[/i] combine with whatever the vehicle touches by the same rule as every PhysX body. Applies to the hull box only -- tire grip is the wheels' own. Unset, the chassis behaves as it always has (friction [code]1.0[/code], bounce [code]0.0[/code]). Changes -- here or to the assigned material -- apply in place without a rebuild and wake the vehicle.

Drive input for the right track, [code]-1[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Same convention as [member left_ratio], applied to the right track's own wheels. Setting [member left_ratio] and [member right_ratio] to opposite signs pivots the vehicle in place.
